# The Workflows operation protocol

In a project where editors cannot write workflow instances directly, an
engine sends each operation to a Workflows service instead, which runs the
verb with the engine and answers with its result. This protocol defines that
exchange. This file is the protocol's ledger: the request and
response shapes, the capabilities read, the error codes, how the service treats
each verb argument, and how a client rebuilds an engine error from a response.

Nothing in this protocol is persisted. Stored document shapes are governed by
[`DATAMODEL.md`](./DATAMODEL.md); this file is versioned by `protocolVersion`
instead. The current version is **1**.

The TypeScript types are exported from `@sanity/workflow-engine`:
`WorkflowOperationRequest`, `WorkflowOperationResponse`,
`WorkflowOperationFailure`, and `WorkflowCapabilities`.

## Transport

Both endpoints are API paths on the engine's client. The engine sends them with
`client.request`, passing a relative `url`:

| Request                  | Method | Body                       | Response                    |
| ------------------------ | ------ | -------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `/workflow/operation`    | `POST` | `WorkflowOperationRequest` | `WorkflowOperationResponse` |
| `/workflow/capabilities` | `GET`  | none                       | `WorkflowCapabilities`      |

`@sanity/client` appends `url` to the client's configured API base URL, so the
request always goes to the API host that client is configured for. The engine
never builds an absolute URL and sets no token or header of its own; the
client's token and headers authenticate the request. A Workflows service you
host is reached through a client configured for that host. With a
`projectId`, `@sanity/client` addresses the project subdomain of `apiHost`, so
set `useProjectHostname: false` to address `apiHost` itself. Either way the
client adds `/v<apiVersion>` before the path, so this client posts operations
to `https://workflows.example.com/v2026-04-29/workflow/operation`:

```ts
import {createClient} from '@sanity/client'

const serviceClient = createClient({
  projectId: 'YOUR_PROJECT_ID',
  dataset: 'production',
  apiVersion: '2026-04-29',
  token: process.env.SANITY_API_TOKEN,
  useCdn: false,
  apiHost: 'https://workflows.example.com',
  useProjectHostname: false,
})
```

`YOUR_PROJECT_ID` is the project the workflows belong to, and
`SANITY_API_TOKEN` holds the editor's token.

A client without `request` cannot send an operation; the transport throws
`ContractViolationError`.

No engine verb sends operations to a service yet. Every verb still writes
directly through the engine's client, whatever host that client addresses.

## Request

```ts
{
  protocolVersion: 1,
  workflowResource: {type: 'dataset', id: 'abc123.production'},
  partition: 'prod',
  verb: 'fireAction',
  args: {instanceId: 'wf-1', activity: 'review', action: 'approve', idempotencyKey: 'k-1'},
  executionContext: {kind: 'studio', id: 'workflow-studio-plugin'},
}
```

| Member             | Meaning                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `protocolVersion`  | Always `1`.                                                                                                                                   |
| `workflowResource` | The engine's `WorkflowResource`, unchanged: the same object as `EngineScopeArgs.workflowResource` and the stored `instance.workflowResource`. |
| `partition`        | The engine's partition.                                                                                                                       |
| `verb`             | One of the verbs below.                                                                                                                       |
| `args`             | The verb's own argument object, unchanged. `instanceId` and `idempotencyKey` travel inside it.                                                |
| `executionContext` | Optional. The sender's `DeclaredExecutionContext`, unchanged. The service uses it for telemetry only; it never affects authorization.         |

The request is a union discriminated on `verb`:

| `verb`          | `args`                                          |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `startInstance` | `StartInstanceArgs`, with `instanceId` required |
| `fireAction`    | `FireActionArgs`                                |
| `editField`     | `EditFieldArgs`                                 |
| `abortInstance` | `AbortInstanceArgs`                             |
| `tick`          | `OperationArgs`                                 |

`startInstance` requires `instanceId` because the client mints the id before
it posts. A retried start with the same id resumes the earlier attempt instead
of creating a second instance.

### Only the per-instance tick crosses the wire

`tick` on the wire is the per-instance verb, `tick({instanceId})`. Choosing
which instances to tick, such as the in-flight query the generated heartbeat in
`createRuntime` runs, is runtime-side work on the deployment's own token. It is
not a protocol verb.

### How the service treats each argument

The service runs the verb with the arguments it honours, exactly as a direct
caller would. A request that sets a rejected member fails with
`operation-malformed` and writes nothing.

| Verb            | Member           | Treatment                                                                                                                    |
| --------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| every verb      | `instanceId`     | Honoured. Required on every verb, `startInstance` included; a request without it is `operation-malformed`.                   |
| every verb      | `grantsFromPath` | Ignored. The service resolves grants on its own side.                                                                        |
| `startInstance` | `definition`     | Honoured.                                                                                                                    |
| `startInstance` | `version`        | Honoured.                                                                                                                    |
| `startInstance` | `initialFields`  | Honoured.                                                                                                                    |
| `startInstance` | `ancestors`      | Honoured.                                                                                                                    |
| `startInstance` | `context`        | Honoured.                                                                                                                    |
| `startInstance` | `perspective`    | Rejected as `operation-malformed`. The service uses the engine's default perspective, as for a direct caller that sets none. |
| `fireAction`    | `idempotencyKey` | Honoured.                                                                                                                    |
| `fireAction`    | `activity`       | Honoured.                                                                                                                    |
| `fireAction`    | `action`         | Honoured.                                                                                                                    |
| `fireAction`    | `params`         | Honoured.                                                                                                                    |
| `fireAction`    | `idempotent`     | Honoured.                                                                                                                    |
| `editField`     | `idempotencyKey` | Honoured.                                                                                                                    |
| `editField`     | `target`         | Honoured.                                                                                                                    |
| `editField`     | `mode`           | Honoured.                                                                                                                    |
| `editField`     | `value`          | Honoured.                                                                                                                    |
| `abortInstance` | `idempotencyKey` | Honoured.                                                                                                                    |
| `abortInstance` | `reason`         | Honoured.                                                                                                                    |

## Response

The service answers every operation with exactly one of two shapes, as a JSON
body:

```ts
{protocolVersion: 1, result: OperationResult}
{protocolVersion: 1, error: WorkflowOperationFailure} // {code: string, message: string, details?: Record<string, unknown>}
```

The body decides the outcome, not the HTTP status. A service answers a result
with `200`; it may answer an error response with any status, such as `409` for
`action-disabled` or `400` for `operation-malformed`. `@sanity/client` rejects
every status of 400 or above, so the client reads the error response from the
rejected request's body and handles it exactly as an error response sent with
`200`. A rejected request whose body is not a protocol version 1 error
response, such as a proxy's `502` page, fails as `operation-transport-failed`.

`result` is the verb's `OperationResult`, unchanged. A response that matches
neither shape, or sets both `result` and `error`, fails as
`operation-response-invalid`; so does a `result.instance` without a string
`_id`. The client reads every other `result.instance` through the engine's
instance read boundary, so an instance from a newer data model fails as
`ModelVersionAheadError` and a malformed one as `PersistedDocShapeError`, as on
a direct read.

## Capabilities

```ts
GET /workflow/capabilities → {modelVersion: number, protocolVersion: number}
```

`modelVersion` is the `DATA_MODEL_VERSION` of the service's engine, the data
model it writes. `protocolVersion` is the highest operation protocol version
the service accepts.

## Error codes

`error.code` is kebab-case. It is one of three kinds of code:

- **An engine error kind.** The verb threw a `WorkflowError`; `code` is its
  `WorkflowErrorKind` and `details` carries its structured fields. The client
  rethrows it as described in the next section.
- **A service code.** The service refused the request itself.
  `operation-malformed` means the request broke this protocol: a missing
  `instanceId`, a rejected argument, or an unknown verb. Further service codes
  are defined with the service.
- **A client code.** The client raises these without a protocol response:
  `operation-transport-failed` when `client.request` rejects without a
  protocol error response in its body, with the transport error as `cause`,
  and `operation-response-invalid` when the
  response does not match protocol version 1.

Service and client codes surface as `WorkflowOperationError`, kind
`operation-failed`, carrying `code`, `message`, and `details`. Only transport,
protocol, and service failures surface that way.

## Rehydration

A client rebuilds an engine error so that every consumer's `instanceof` check
and field read behaves as on a direct call. For an error response, the client
looks `code` up in the map below.

- **A mapped class.** `details` must carry every field the class requires,
  each with the JSON type the map lists. A response with a field missing or of
  the wrong type fails as `operation-response-invalid` instead of producing a
  half-built error. The client then creates an instance of the class without
  running its constructor, so the service's `message` and fields arrive
  unchanged. It sets `kind` to `code` and `name` to the class name, and copies
  every `details` member onto the error as an own field, except `kind`, `name`,
  `message`, and `stack`. The envelope `message` is always the error's
  message; a `details.message` never replaces it. Two members are restored
  rather than copied:
  - `details.cause` is `{message, statusCode?}` and becomes an `Error` with
    that message and status code, so cause checks such as
    `isRevisionConflict` read it as on a direct call.
  - `details.instance` is read through the engine's instance read boundary,
    with the same failures as `result.instance`.
- **What the client does not check.** It checks each required field's JSON
  type only, not the structure inside an object or array field, and copies
  optional and unlisted `details` members unchecked. A service on a newer
  engine may add members or nest new ones inside a listed field, and a client
  that predates them still rebuilds the error instead of failing. A consumer
  that reads inside a field, such as `reason` or `issues`, must tolerate
  members it does not know.
- **`WorkflowOperationError`, or a code not in the map.** The client throws
  `WorkflowOperationError` with the response's `code`, `message`, and `details`.

The map in code is total over `WorkflowErrorKind`, and its required fields are
derived from each class: a kind added to the engine, or a required field added
to a mapped class, fails typecheck until the map covers it. Update this table
in the same change.

| `code`                        | Rethrown as                     | Required `details` fields                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `abort-denied`                | `AbortDeniedError`              | `reason` (object)                                                                                                     |
| `action-disabled`             | `ActionDisabledError`           | `reason` (object), `activity` (string), `action` (string)                                                             |
| `action-params-invalid`       | `ActionParamsInvalidError`      | `action` (string), `activity` (string), `issues` (array)                                                              |
| `cascade-limit`               | `CascadeLimitError`             | `instanceId` (string), `limit` (number)                                                                               |
| `concurrent-cascade`          | `ConcurrentCascadeError`        | `instanceId` (string), `attempts` (number)                                                                            |
| `concurrent-edit-field`       | `ConcurrentEditFieldError`      | `instanceId` (string), `target` (object), `attempts` (number)                                                         |
| `concurrent-fire-action`      | `ConcurrentFireActionError`     | `instanceId` (string), `activity` (string), `action` (string), `attempts` (number)                                    |
| `contract-violation`          | `ContractViolationError`        | none                                                                                                                  |
| `definition-not-found`        | `DefinitionNotFoundError`       | `definition` (string)                                                                                                 |
| `edit-field-denied`           | `EditFieldDeniedError`          | `reason` (object), `target` (object)                                                                                  |
| `field-value-shape`           | `FieldValueShapeError`          | `entryType` (string), `entryName` (string), `issues` (array)                                                          |
| `initial-fields-invalid`      | `InitialFieldsInvalidError`     | `issues` (array)                                                                                                      |
| `instance-not-found`          | `InstanceNotFoundError`         | `instanceId` (string)                                                                                                 |
| `model-version-ahead`         | `ModelVersionAheadError`        | `documentId` (string), `documentModelVersion` (number), `requiredReaderModel` (number), `engineModelVersion` (number) |
| `mutation-guard-denied`       | `MutationGuardDeniedError`      | `denied` (array), `documentId` (string), `action` (string)                                                            |
| `persisted-doc-shape`         | `PersistedDocShapeError`        | `documentId` (string), `documentType` (string), `issues` (array)                                                      |
| `ref-resource-undeclared`     | `RefResourceUndeclaredError`    | `entryType` (string), `entryName` (string), `issues` (array)                                                          |
| `required-field-not-provided` | `RequiredFieldNotProvidedError` | `missing` (array)                                                                                                     |
| `start-not-allowed`           | `StartNotAllowedError`          | `definition` (string), `unmetRequirements` (array)                                                                    |
| `start-not-primed`            | `StartNotPrimedError`           | `instanceId` (string)                                                                                                 |
| `start-not-settled`           | `StartNotSettledError`          | `instanceId` (string)                                                                                                 |
| `workflow-state-diverged`     | `WorkflowStateDivergedError`    | `instanceId` (string)                                                                                                 |

These kinds map to `WorkflowOperationError`, because no protocol verb throws
them:

| `code`                         | Why it never crosses the wire                                               |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `concurrent-commit-effect-ops` | Effect reporting is not a protocol verb.                                    |
| `concurrent-complete-effect`   | Effect completion is not a protocol verb.                                   |
| `effect-commit-queue-overflow` | Effect reporting is not a protocol verb.                                    |
| `effect-not-found`             | Effect completion is not a protocol verb.                                   |
| `effect-ops-invalid`           | Effect completion and reporting are not protocol verbs.                     |
| `effect-outputs-invalid`       | Effect completion is not a protocol verb.                                   |
| `missing-effect-handler`       | Effect draining is not a protocol verb.                                     |
| `stale-effect-claim`           | Effect reporting is not a protocol verb.                                    |
| `definition-in-use`            | Deleting definitions is not a protocol verb.                                |
| `reader-model-acknowledgement` | Deploying definitions is not a protocol verb.                               |
| `spawn-contracts-invalid`      | Deploying definitions is not a protocol verb.                               |
| `unknown-project-roles`        | Deploying definitions is not a protocol verb.                               |
| `partial-guard-deploy`         | Every verb's guard commit turns it into `workflow-state-diverged` first.    |
| `operation-failed`             | A client-side kind. A service reports its own failures under service codes. |
